evidence: Reviewed staged diff in MyAccessibilityService.kt: removed the top-40-percent band filter from findAndClickCloseButton so every blank ImageView inside the resolved scope competes in one ranking (clickable rank first, then rightmost, then topmost); stage labels in candidatos and elegido logs simplified to popup or ventana; KDoc rewritten to document the Compose flat-tree reason - the in-app popup has no card container so scope equals the full screen, the X sits about 62 percent down and the old band admitted the centered chevron while excluding the X, producing a click on the chevron on the first attempt; build.gradle.kts version bump to 0.3.46

aapt dump badging reports com.example.projectacc versionCode 61 versionName 0.3.46; compileDebugKotlin succeeded with no warnings; device logs from v0.3.45 show the band pool contained only the chevron at top 538 while the X at top 982 was unreachable, and the full-popup pool ranked the X at right 666 over the chevron at right 440 and closed successfully

findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt findAndClickCloseButton ranking over the whole scope
findings.claim: Removing the band means the first attempt now evaluates the same candidate set that previously only attempt two saw, so the X at right 666 with clickable rank 2 beats the centered chevron at right 440 with the same rank on rightness alone, eliminating the wasted first attempt against the chevron. The residual risk is a clickable blank ImageView further right than the X inside the same scope - none appeared in the recorded candidate dumps for either mode, the 300 ms verification converts a wrong pick into a retried CLICK_FAILED, and the full candidate list in logcat would expose such a competitor immediately.
proof_refs: device log attempt one shows the band pool with only the chevron at top 538 left 280 right 440 and the popup staying open after click
device log attempt two shows the full popup pool with the X at right 666 beating the chevron at right 440 and closing verified

findings.claim: In app mode findPopupContainer cannot isolate the offer card because Picap renders a flattened Compose semantics tree where the X, the chevron and Aceptar are siblings; the outermost inset ancestor containing an ID node ends up being the content frame at nearly full-screen bounds, so scope degrades to the whole screen and the scope label in the logs reads popup even though it equals the window. This is tolerable now that ranking alone decides and the outside-app mode still benefits from window equals card, but any future scope-based heuristic would inherit the same imprecision in app mode; improving it would require a non-structural anchor such as the topmost card text row.
proof_refs: device log scope rect 0 0 to 720 1520 against window rect 0 0 to 720 1600 in app mode shows the scope covering virtually the entire window
device log outside the app shows scope equal to the window and a single successful pick with label ventana
